title: Overview: choose the structure
question: Same content, new look. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Leaders first
options.lineage: A leaderboard that names its winner
options.thesis: Each ranking opens with its leader at full size (name, rate, the work behind it), then the rest as ruled rows; phone closers and top posts share the row below.
materials: navy band with the date picker
options.viewport: Navy band (Overview, the range in words, live line, Today / This week / This month / Custom range); three ranking cards, leader at 32px, ranks 2–5 at 17px, total and Show all in the footer; then the phone closers table beside top posts with thumbnails.
options.risk: The leader block rewards one person loudly; on a quiet day it crowns someone at 0.4/h.

options.label: Posts lead
options.lineage: A content wall with the team in a rail
options.thesis: Top posts and reels own the main column as a picture wall (the top post large, four more beside it); the three rankings stack in a right rail like Today's.
options.viewport: Navy band with the picker; left, a Top posts card (one 250px tile with caption, handle, submissions and people; a 2×2 grid of smaller tiles); phone closers table under it; right, a 384px rail of Lead Gen, Top Qualifiers and Top DM Closers, top three each.
options.risk: Puts content above people: the team's numbers drop to a rail, and with no previews yet the wall is grey tiles.

options.label: Team tables
options.lineage: One per-person table recipe, four times
options.thesis: A strip of the team totals, then every team as the same ruled table (rank, person, output, hours, a rate bar), so the four read as one system and become the recipe the Operations pages reuse.
options.viewport: Navy band with the picker; a white strip of five totals (submissions, qualified, booked by DM closers, calls booked, show rate); a 2×2 grid of tables: Lead Gen, Top Qualifiers, Top DM Closers, Phone closers; top posts below the fold as rows with thumbnails.
options.risk: The most uniform: posts fall below the first screen, and four equal tables give the eye no lead.
